title: kernel-v1 fault-test evidence (v1)
description: Structured result of a single auth/durability/protocol fault-injection case (SPIRE SVID rotation, OIDC/RBAC negative, gRPC backpressure, Kafka/ClickHouse durability, LSM fail-open, etc.). Each row binds the unit under test, the injected fault, the expected behaviour, the observed behaviour, a pass/fail verdict, and an optional replay command so a reviewer can reproduce the exact case.

schema_version.description: Bumped on backward-incompatible shape changes. Currently always 1.

kind.description: Fault-test class. Stable set: spire_svid_rotation, oidc_rbac, grpc_backpressure, kafka_durability, clickhouse_durability, sqlcipher_durability, lsm_fail_open, policy_replay, policy_stale, policy_disconnect, ring_full, loader_crash, service_restart, host_reboot, rollback.

subject.description: The unit under test. Always an object so later tests can add fields without bumping the schema.

cluster.description: Cluster identifier when the subject is per-cluster.

fault.description: Injected fault. 'kind' is a stable token (e.g. 'kill_broker', 'revoke_svid', 'partition_stream', 'fill_disk'); 'params' carries fault-kind-specific arguments. The pair (kind, params) MUST be enough for the replay_cmd to reproduce the case.

params.description: Free-form parameters for the fault. Schema intentionally loose to accommodate new fault kinds without bumping the version.

expected.description: Expected outcome as a stable string (e.g. 'deny_disabled_within_5000ms', 'grpc_deadline_observed', 'replay_rejected_with_stale_digest', 'rollback_converges_to_lkg'). Reviewers MUST be able to test the observed string against this expectation without parsing natural language.

observed.description: Observed outcome as a stable string. Must be one of the strings documented for the fault kind so a reviewer can compare them by exact-match.

pass_fail.description: True iff observed satisfies the contract documented for (kind, expected). The test runner is responsible for the comparison; reviewers can re-run replay_cmd to verify.

replay_cmd.description: Optional shell command that, when executed, reproduces the fault and observes the same outcome. Reviewers re-run this in CI to prove the verdict is not flaky.
